# Environmental Gram-negatives: pseudomonads, vibrios and Burkholderia

> *What happens when bacteria adapted to water and soil meet a human host?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the same template as the *Gram-positive cocci* chapter. The outline below
shows what it will cover.
:::

**The group in one sentence:** Gram-negative rods that live in water, soil and the sea, hardy and naturally resistant to many chemicals.

**How members differ (the sorting key):** Must respire or can ferment; salt tolerance; where in the environment they live.

**Main organisms (full profile cards):** *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* (water, natural resistance), *Burkholderia pseudomallei* (soil, diabetes as host factor, Singapore relevance), *Vibrio cholerae* (a single toxin).

**Supporting organisms (one table row each):** *Vibrio vulnificus*, *Vibrio parahaemolyticus*.

**Later in the course:** Hospital infections, melioidosis and cholera in the organ blocks.
